intro: An AI study buddy for Mac is a voice assistant that sees your screen and answers out loud. Lazur is one. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask about the paragraph or diagram in front of you, in plain words. It sets reminders for due dates, starts study timers and dictates notes with fn in any app. It runs on Mac only, and it works best as a tutor, not a ghostwriter.
tldr: Hold ⌥ ⌘ on a lecture slide and ask for it explained in plain words.
Say 'remind me the essay is due Friday' and it lands in Apple Reminders.
Dictate lecture notes with fn in Google Docs, Notion or Word.
Pro is $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually. The trial is 3 days, with no credit card.

painPoints.title: Messages take most of the day
painPoints.text: Microsoft found that the average Microsoft 365 employee spent 57% of time on meetings, email and chat in 2023. No study we found measures this for students. Your inbox, class portal and group chat probably work the same way.

painPoints.title: Dense readings that take many passes
painPoints.text: One paragraph can take several reads before the point lands. You lose time on the same sentence while the rest of the chapter waits. Homework and research averages 0.20 hours a day for all adults in 2025, per the BLS.

painPoints.title: Games and feeds on the same laptop
painPoints.text: Leisure computer use, including games and social media, rose to 37 minutes a day in 2025. It was 25 minutes in 2015. The same laptop holds your reading, your notes and your feed.

painPoints.title: A new tool in every course
painPoints.text: Each course has its own portal, templates and tools. Each one hides its settings in a new menu. Minutes go to hunting for the right menu, not to the work itself.

faq.question: Is there a student discount?
faq.answer: This page does not list a student price, so check the [pricing page](/pricing) for current offers. Pro is $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually, with 250 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both plans.

faq.question: Does Lazur work in every app?
faq.answer: It works on top of any Mac app, because it sees the screen. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app. It does not click buttons or operate apps for you. It guides you one click at a time instead.

faq.question: Is it always listening?
faq.answer: No. It listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Can it set deadline reminders?
faq.answer: Yes. Say something like 'remind me the essay is due Friday at 5 PM' and the reminder goes to Apple Reminders. Check the date once, the first time you use it, so you know it heard you right.

faq.question: Will it write my essay?
faq.answer: Lazur can draft short text, but that does not mean you should hand it in. Your instructor sets the rules for each assignment. Use Lazur to understand the material, then write the work yourself.

faq.question: Does it work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: Does it work with Google Docs, Notion and Word?
faq.answer: It works in any app you have open, including Google Docs, Notion and Word. See [Google Docs for students](/for/students/google-docs), [Notion for students](/for/students/notion) and [Word for students](/for/students/word).

blocks.text: What an AI study buddy for Mac does on a school day

Most of the help you need is small. A paragraph that will not make sense. A slide with too many arrows. A deadline you forgot to write down. An AI study buddy for Mac handles each of these in seconds, out loud, without you leaving the app you have open.
Lazur does five things for students. You trigger most of them by holding ⌥ ⌘, or by holding fn for dictation.

items: Explain: hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask about a paragraph, figure or slide. Lazur answers out loud.
Point: ask where a menu or button is. Lazur circles it and adds a label.
Guide: ask how to do a task. Lazur walks you through it one click at a time and waits for each click.
Everyday: reminders, timers, Calendar events, notes, music, opening apps and links.
Dictate and draft: hold fn to type text at the cursor. Lazur drafts short text you check before you send.

blocks.text: Explain a dense reading in plain words

Start with one paragraph, not the whole chapter. Keep the paragraph on screen and hold ⌥ ⌘. Ask a narrow question, such as 'what is the main claim here?' A narrow question gets a short answer you can use in your notes.

Here is a worked example. You open a sociology article in Chrome. A paragraph uses the word 'hegemony' three times and never defines it. You hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask what it means in this paragraph. Lazur answers out loud, using the context on screen. Then you ask what the author is arguing against. Two questions usually do the job.
Check every answer against the text. Lazur reads what is on screen, so it cannot explain a page you have not scrolled to. If the paragraph is cut off, scroll first, then ask again.

blocks.title: Try it yourself first
blocks.text: Say the point in your own words before you ask. Then ask Lazur to check what you said. A check shows you the gap. A copied answer hides it.
Explain a diagram or lecture slide on screen

Diagrams are where an AI study buddy earns its keep. Lazur reads the labels, arrows and layout on screen and explains the process out loud. Ask it to go left to right, or top to bottom, to match the slide. Biology, chemistry and engineering courses lean on diagrams, so this helps most there.

Keep deadlines in Reminders, not in your head

Due dates pile up across courses and apps. Lazur adds them to Apple Reminders by voice. Say the deadline the way you would say it to a friend, with the day and the time. Then check the date in Reminders, because a fast sentence can be misheard.
Add a deadline by voice, step by step

items: Keep the page or email with the due date on screen.
Say: remind me the essay is due Friday at 5 PM.
Open Apple Reminders and confirm the day and time.
When you start studying, say: timer for 50 minutes, study.

blocks.text: The common mistake is saying 'Friday' with no time. A date without a time can leave the reminder vague. Say the time every time. If several classes have essays due the same week, say the course name too.
Use Calendar for class times and exams. Use Reminders for due dates and small to-dos. One home for each type saves you from checking several apps before you start.
Take notes by voice with fn in Google Docs, Notion or Word

Typing lecture notes is slow, and your hands tire on long days. Hold fn and speak. Lazur dictates clean, formatted text at the cursor, in any app. Google Docs, Notion and Word all take it, because the text goes to whichever app has focus.

Dictation has three extras that help with coursework. Snippets expand a short phrase into longer text. A personal dictionary keeps course names and technical terms right. Clipboard slots hold text you need to paste later. Dictation is unlimited on both plans.

A simple workflow works well. Dictate a summary right after class, while the lecture is fresh. Then open the reading and ask Lazur to point at the sections you missed. Write the summary in your own words, because that is what you will study from.

Setup differs by app. For Docs, see [Google Docs for students on Mac](/for/students/google-docs). For Notion, see [Notion for students on Mac](/for/students/notion). For writing-heavy work, see [dictation for writers on Mac](/for/writers).
Where your study time goes, and what the numbers say
No study we found measures how students spend time on computers or in email. The figures below describe all adults and office workers. Read them as a trend, not as a picture of your week.

The BLS figures cover all civilian adults. Homework and research averaged 0.20 hours a day in 2025. Attending class averaged 0.21 hours a day. Leisure computer use rose to 37 minutes a day, up from 25 minutes in 2015. The same laptop runs your reading and your feed.

The Microsoft chart shows where office workers spend app time. Meetings and chat take the most. Word takes 10%. Your own split will look different, so check it. Open System Settings > Screen Time to see which apps take your hours.
Use it to understand the work, not to hand it in

An AI study buddy works like a tutor on your screen. It explains a concept more than one way and checks your reasoning. It should not write the answer you hand in, unless your instructor allows it. Your school sets the rules on AI, and those rules can change from one course to the next.

blocks.title: Read the rule before you ask
blocks.text: Check the syllabus and the assignment page before you use AI on graded work. If the rule is unclear, ask your instructor in writing. Lazur does not know your course rules.

Good tutoring questions sound like this: 'where did I go wrong in this proof?' or 'is my argument in this paragraph clear?' Weak questions sound like 'do my problem set.' The first kind builds the skill. The second kind skips it.
What Lazur does not do for you
Lazur guides and points. You do the clicks and the typing. That keeps you in control of your files and your coursework.

items: Lazur does not click buttons for you.
Lazur does not edit files for you.
Lazur does not operate other apps for you.
Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app.

blocks.text: Check your Mac apps before a deadline

Software changes every term. Check your versions before you follow a guide, because menus move. Pages 15.1 requires macOS 15.6 Sequoia or later. Pages 14.5 supports macOS 14.0 Sonoma and later. Apple's Pages user guide covers Pages 15.4.

Word for Mac is at version 16.114.3, released October 27, 2026. The release notes list quality and performance improvements, with no new features. If a menu looks different from the guide, ask Lazur to point at it.

Pages, Keynote and Numbers are free to use. Some extras need an Apple subscription, including AI image generation and Keynote's automatic presentation creation. Without a subscription, Content Hub items carry a watermark.

items: Find your macOS version: Apple menu > About This Mac.
Match the app version to the guide before you follow steps.
Ask Lazur to point at a menu if your version looks different.

blocks.text: Mail's user guide is titled for macOS 27. If your Mac runs an older release, some menus may differ from the guide. Read the menu bar before you follow a step.
Mistakes students make with an AI study buddy

items: Asking about the whole chapter at once. Ask about one paragraph or one figure instead.
Trusting an answer without checking the text. Scroll to the part you need first.
Skipping the notes step. Dictate a summary right after class, while it is fresh.
Leaving a deadline out of Reminders. Add it the moment you see it.
Using it in place of your instructor. Ask them when the rules are unclear.
